standard_prerequisites.name: Formal unramifiedness is local on source and target
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Morphisms, Stacks tag 02HC (more-morphisms-lemma-formally-unramified-on-opens), invoked at proof line 1086
standard_prerequisites.use: Keeps each Z_i to U_i formally unramified for an affine open covering Z = union Z_i with Z_i mapping into an affine open U_i of X, which is what makes the affine case applicable piece by piece.

core_obligations: Extract from the defining lifting property the two facts the glueing needs: a universal first order thickening is unique up to unique isomorphism, and for open subschemes V in Z and U in X with h(V) contained in U the open subscheme V' of Z' with V = Z cap V' is the universal first order thickening of V over U (proof lines 1040-1061).

Settle the affine case completely: starting from the algebra lemma for affine test diagrams, extend the universal property to an arbitrary diagram T in T' over X by covering T' by affine opens, producing morphisms a'_i over X that agree on affine opens of the intersections by uniqueness, and gluing them to a global a' (proof lines 1063-1081).

Glue the affine pieces and descend the universal property: choose an affine open covering Z = union Z_i with Z_i mapping into an affine open U_i, obtain universal thickenings Z_i in Z'_i over U_i, identify both Z'_{i,j} and Z'_{j,i} as the universal first order thickening of Z_i cap Z_j over X so that the transition isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle condition on triple overlaps, glue to Z in Z' over X, and verify that local universality for diagrams whose image lies in some Z_i implies the universal property for an arbitrary diagram by covering T' so that the image of T_i lands in Z_i (proof lines 1083-1126).
proof_roadmap: General remarks: uniqueness up to unique isomorphism, and the localisation statement for open V in Z over U in X, proved by pushing a diagram for V and U into the universal property of Z' and using that T and T' have the same underlying topological space (proof lines 1040-1061).

Affine case: with X = Spec(R) and Z = Spec(S), the algebra lemma gives Z in Z' over X universal for affine test diagrams; an arbitrary diagram is handled by an affine open covering T' = union T'_i, whose local solutions agree on overlaps by uniqueness and therefore glue (proof lines 1063-1081).

Glueing: pick an affine open covering Z = union Z_i with Z_i inside an affine open U_i of X, use that Z_i to U_i stays formally unramified, invoke the affine case, and observe that each Z_i in Z'_i is then universal over X as well (proof lines 1083-1090).

Cocycle: the two open subschemes Z'_{i,j} and Z'_{j,i} of Z'_i and Z'_j are both universal first order thickenings of Z_i cap Z_j over X, hence canonically isomorphic; the cocycle condition on Z'_{i,j} cap Z'_{i,k} follows from the same uniqueness (proof lines 1091-1101).

Descent of the universal property: glue along the transition isomorphisms, then for an arbitrary diagram cover T' so that a(T_i) lies in Z_i, obtain local morphisms a'_i, observe that on T'_i cap T'_j any two solutions map into the universal thickening Z'_i cap Z'_j of Z_i cap Z_j over X and hence coincide, and glue to a' (proof lines 1102-1126).
difficulty_reason: The statement asserts that a formally unramified morphism h : Z to X admits a first order thickening Z in Z' that is universal for all diagrams T in T' over X (statement lines 1026-1028), an object defined by a lifting property rather than constructed by a formula. The proof is a construction with a chain of genuinely separate steps: it first derives uniqueness and the localisation of the universal property for open subschemes from the definition (proof lines 1040-1061), then upgrades the algebra lemma from affine test diagrams to arbitrary ones by an affine open covering of T' and a glueing with uniqueness (proof lines 1063-1081), then produces the global Z' by glueing affine pieces along open subschemes that are identified as universal thickenings of the intersections, which is what yields the cocycle condition (proof lines 1083-1101). The final and least formal step is the descent of the universal property itself: local universality on a cover of Z has to be converted into the lifting property for an arbitrary diagram, which is done by covering T' so that each a(T_i) lands in some Z_i and then comparing two solutions through the universal thickening of Z_i cap Z_j (proof lines 1108-1126). Formal unramifiedness is consumed at exactly one point, proof line 1086.
